displacement.source: Operating condition (about half deadweight): 2 demihulls x 28.1 m LWL x 2.7 m waterline beam x 1.0 m hull draft x block coefficient 0.52 at 1020 kg/m3
displacement.note: Ask crew or the operator for the lightship and loaded displacement.

engineModel.note: Delivered as EPA Tier 3; Tier 4 repower with SCR reported (marinelog-k-class-repower).

gearRatio.source: ZF 3050 standard ratio (catalogue range 1.5 to 2.95) giving about 840 propeller rpm at 2100 engine rpm, as on the T-class (2.519)
gearRatio.note: Ask crew or the shipyard for the ratio plate.

propellerDiameter.source: 42 in, as on the deep-draft Rockaway T-class variant with the same engine family at similar power; fits the 0.6 m between hull and maximum draft
propellerDiameter.note: Ask crew or Michigan Wheel for the propeller size and pitch.

yawRadiusOfGyration.source: About 0.26 x LOA: 0.25 L for the hull mass along its length plus the demihulls' lateral offset (catamaran mass sits outboard)

longitudinalCentreOfGravity.source: LCG about 45% of the waterline length from its aft end, typical of fast ferries with engines aft

centreOfGravityHeight.source: KG about 3.4 m for a two-deck aluminium ferry, less the hull draft

demihullSeparation.source: Overall beam less one demihull beam (8.5 - 2.7 m), centreline to centreline

demihullBeam.source: Waterline beam that, with a demihull block coefficient of 0.52, floats the estimated displacement at the published hull draft

midshipSectionArea.source: 2 x demihull beam x hull draft x midship coefficient 0.72 (round bilge)

wettedSurface.source: 2 x 2.7 x sqrt(demihull volume x LWL), the usual coefficient for slender round-bilge demihulls

formFactor.source: (1 + beta k) of round-bilge catamarans at s/L about 0.2 to 0.25 including viscous interference, typical of the Insel and Molland (1992) tests

correlationAllowance.source: Typical roughness and correlation allowance for a painted aluminium hull in service

residuaryResistanceScale.source: Set so that full power (2 x 999 kW at 2100 rpm) gives the published 30.0 kn maximum in calm deep water
residuaryResistanceScale.note: Calibration parameter: refit from AIS speed-power data and crew rpm-speed figures.

asternResistanceFactor.source: Transom-first running of a fast catamaran: immersed transom leading and the fine bow trailing, roughly 2 to 3 times ahead resistance
asternResistanceFactor.note: Ask crew: boat speed going astern at a given rpm.

surgeAddedMass.source: About 5% of displacement for slender hulls (Motora charts give 2% to 6%)

swayAddedMass.source: Strip theory: double-body sway added mass of a rectangular section (DNV-RP-C205 coefficient about 1.2 with rounded bilges) x 0.85 effective length, both demihulls

yawAddedInertia.source: Strip theory: each demihull's sway added mass distributed over its length (L^2/12 x 0.8 for tapered ends), both demihulls

derivativeYv.source: Clarke, Gedling and Hine (1983) linear-derivative regressions for one demihull (T/L 0.036, B/T 2.7, CB 0.52) on the MMG basis, x 2 demihulls x 1.2 catamaran interaction (Duman and Bal 2022 CFD for the Delft 372 catamaran gives Y'v -0.39 to -0.58)

derivativeYr.source: Clarke, Gedling and Hine (1983) linear-derivative regressions for one demihull (T/L 0.036, B/T 2.7, CB 0.52) on the MMG basis, x 2 demihulls x 1.2 catamaran interaction (Duman and Bal 2022 CFD for the Delft 372 catamaran gives Y'v -0.39 to -0.58)

derivativeNv.source: Clarke, Gedling and Hine (1983) linear-derivative regressions for one demihull (T/L 0.036, B/T 2.7, CB 0.52) on the MMG basis, x 2 demihulls x 1.2 catamaran interaction (Duman and Bal 2022 CFD for the Delft 372 catamaran gives Y'v -0.39 to -0.58)

derivativeNr.source: Clarke, Gedling and Hine (1983) linear-derivative regressions for one demihull (T/L 0.036, B/T 2.7, CB 0.52) on the MMG basis, x 2 demihulls x 1.2 catamaran interaction (Duman and Bal 2022 CFD for the Delft 372 catamaran gives Y'v -0.39 to -0.58)

derivativeXvv.source: Induced drag in drift: KVLCC2 MMG value -0.040 (Yasukawa and Yoshimura 2015), Delft 372 catamaran CFD -0.18 (Duman and Bal 2022)

derivativeXvr.source: Hydrodynamic part taken as zero; the added-mass term (m + m_y) v r is in the equations of motion

derivativeXrr.source: Taken as zero, small for slender demihulls

crossFlowDragCoefficient.source: Sectional cross-flow drag of round-bilge sections of order 0.6 to 1.0 (Hoerner 1965), reduced for the downstream demihull sitting in the upstream one's wake

lateralForceDepth.source: Centre of lateral pressure taken at half the hull draft

pitchRatio.source: B-series P/D at which the propeller absorbs rated power at rated rpm at the 30.0 kn published maximum (J 0.992); fast-ferry propellers are usually P/D 1.1 to 1.4
pitchRatio.note: Calibration parameter: confirm from the propeller maker's drawing or the boat's rpm-speed curve.

expandedAreaRatio.source: Five-blade NiBrAl propellers for 25 to 30 kn ferries typically have AE/A0 0.75 to 0.9 for cavitation margin

longitudinalPosition.source: About 1.3 m forward of the aft end of the waterline

shaftDepth.source: Maximum draft less half the propeller diameter

wakeFraction.source: Fast catamarans with propellers under the demihulls have small effective wake, about 0.0 to 0.06

thrustDeduction.source: Typical for twin-screw fast craft, 0.04 to 0.1

asternThrustDeduction.source: Astern jet runs forward along the demihull; larger deduction than ahead

reversedFlowLiftFactor.source: Chosen so astern bollard thrust is about 0.7 of ahead (fixed-pitch propellers typically give 0.6 to 0.75)

bladeNormalDragCoefficient.source: Flat-plate normal-force coefficient of low-aspect-ratio blades; Hausler et al. (2013) fit 1.04 for a Ka 4-70 propeller

rotation.source: Usual arrangement on twin-screw ferries; ask crew (reference kit: prop walk)

propWalkAhead.source: Small paddle-wheel side force under a slender demihull, 1% to 3% of thrust

propWalkAstern.source: Astern walk is several times stronger than ahead walk on shaft-driven boats, 4% to 8% of thrust

shaftInertia.source: Propeller (0.05 m D^2 for a 180 kg NiBrAl wheel) plus 25% entrained water plus shaft and gear output

shaftFrictionTorque.source: Shaft bearings, stern seal and gearbox output drag, about 1% of full-power shaft torque

slipstreamFactor.source: MMG kappa, 0.5 to 0.6 for a rudder about one diameter behind the propeller (Yasukawa and Yoshimura 2015 use 0.50)

upstreamInflowFactor.source: Actuator-disc induction one diameter upstream of the disc is about a tenth of the far-wake speed-up

idleSpeed.source: Baudouin 12M26.3 datasheet idle speed; vessel setting unconfirmed
idleSpeed.note: Ask crew: engine rpm at idle in gear.

frictionTorqueAtIdle.source: About 4% of rated torque at idle

frictionTorqueAtRatedSpeed.source: About 10% of rated torque (mechanical efficiency about 0.9 at rated speed)

governorTimeConstant.source: Stiff electronic speed governor: full fuel for a few percent speed error, so rpm response is set by torque, boost and inertia

governorIntegralTime.source: Integral time of the PI speed governor, removing droop within about a second

unboostedTorqueFraction.source: Torque available before the turbocharger spools up, about half of full load

turbochargerTimeConstant.source: Turbocharger spool-up lag of high-speed marine diesels, about 1 to 2 s
turbochargerTimeConstant.note: Ask crew: seconds from idle to full rpm in gear.

gearEfficiency.source: Marine reverse-reduction gears transmit 96% to 98% of input power

clutchTorqueCapacity.source: Twice the engine's peak torque at the output shaft (gear ratio 2.5), the usual service-factor margin of a ZF 3050

clutchFillTime.source: Solenoid and clutch fill delay of ZF hydraulic gears, a few tenths of a second
clutchFillTime.note: Ask crew: time from lever into gear to the clutch biting.

clutchEngagementTime.source: Clutch pressure ramp from first contact to full pressure on ZF hydraulic gears

clutchReleaseTime.source: Hydraulic clutch release, quicker than the fill (oil dumps to drain)

clutchInLever.source: Idle detent at about 12% of lever travel on single-lever control heads
clutchInLever.note: Ask crew: where the ahead and astern idle detents are.

throttleStartLever.source: Throttle begins to open just past the detent

detentHysteresis.source: Keeps a noisy input device from chattering at the detent

neutralDwell.source: Electronic controls hold neutral for a programmable delay when reversing, typically a few seconds; 2 s assumed
neutralDwell.note: Ask crew: time from ahead idle to astern engaged.

throttlePause.source: Throttle held at idle briefly after the clutch engages; installers can set this pause on electronic controls

shiftInterlockSpeed.source: Clutch engagement inhibited until the engine is near idle

steeringMode.source: Wheel position orders rudder angle; ask crew whether the helm is follow-up or a non-follow-up jog lever

hardOverAngle.note: Ask crew: rudder angle at hard over.

steeringRate.source: Hard over to hard over in about 10 s, typical of electro-hydraulic steering on 25 to 30 m fast craft (SOLAS II-1/29 minimum for ships is 35 to 30 deg in 28 s)
steeringRate.note: Ask crew: seconds from hard over to hard over.

area.source: About 1.7% of one demihull's L x T, above the DNV minimum (T L / 100)(1 + 25 (B/L)^2) for each hull

aspectRatio.source: Spade rudder sized to the space under the transom

longitudinalPosition.source: About 0.6 m aft of the propellers

stallAngle.source: Stall of a low-aspect-ratio rudder in propeller wash, 30 to 40 deg

reversedFlowLiftFactor.source: Trailing-edge-first lift slope of NACA-type sections is about half of normal flow

flowStraightening.source: MMG gamma_R, 0.4 to 0.65 (Yasukawa and Yoshimura 2015 KVLCC2: 0.395 and 0.640)

effectiveLeverFactor.source: MMG l'_R, -0.7 to -1.0 (Yasukawa and Yoshimura 2015 KVLCC2: -0.710)

slipstreamSpanFraction.source: Propeller diameter larger than the rudder span, rudder partly above the inclined jet

wakeRatio.source: MMG epsilon close to 1 for small wake fractions

hullLateralInteraction.source: MMG a_H; small for a slender demihull (0.2 to 0.4 for full monohulls)

hullInteractionPosition.source: MMG x'_H, about -0.45 (Yasukawa and Yoshimura 2015 KVLCC2: -0.464)

dragDeduction.source: MMG t_R, 0.2 to 0.4 (Yasukawa and Yoshimura 2015 KVLCC2: 0.387)

forceDepth.source: Centre of the rudder span below the waterline

frontalArea.source: Beam x freeboard plus two cabin decks and wheelhouse from published photographs; confirm from the general arrangement

lateralArea.source: Length x freeboard plus superstructure profile from published photographs; confirm from the general arrangement

lateralCoefficient.source: Fossen (2011) c_y range 0.70 to 0.95 for ships with superstructure

yawCoefficient.source: Fossen (2011) c_n range 0.05 to 0.20 for ships with superstructure

lateralAreaCentre.source: Wheelhouse and upper deck slightly forward of midships

lateralAreaHeight.source: Centroid of the profile above the waterline

hullFenderStiffness.source: Assumed continuous rubber fender (rubbing strake) along the sheer, across the bow and the transoms, as on harbour ferries that berth against fendered barges: a hollow D section about 200 mm deep gives about 350 kN per metre at 0.10 m compression
hullFenderStiffness.note: Ask crew: section, size and material of the hull fendering (reference kit: fenders).

hullFenderDamping.source: Rubber hysteresis as a damping time c/k of 0.02 s on the stiffness above: a loss factor of about 0.2 at the 10 rad/s of a fender contact

hullFenderMaxCompression.source: About half the depth of a 200 mm hollow D fender, its usual rated deflection

bottomedStiffnessFactor.source: Past a fender's compression limit the aluminium hull and the landing structure take the load: 20 times the fender stiffness stops a 6 kn head-on impact within centimetres and stays accurate in the 1 ms contact substeps

fenderHysteresis.source: Engineering estimate: elastomeric fenders return less energy on recovery than they absorb in compression (loading and unloading hysteresis); 0.2 makes the loading force 1.2 and the unloading force 0.8 times the elastic law, a loss of about a third of the energy per cycle. Lumps the barge fender's and the hull fendering's rubber together until landing data or crew input says otherwise
fenderHysteresis.note: Ask crew: how far a boat bounces back off the barge after a firm landing in neutral.

blockageCoefficient.source: Lackenby (1963) shallow-water speed-loss formula, potential-flow term 0.1242 (A_X/h^2 - 0.05)

criticalSpeedAmplitude.source: Residuary resistance peaks near depth Froude number 1 in shallow water (Millward 1983); amplitude for these hulls uncertain
criticalSpeedAmplitude.note: Calibration parameter: fit from AIS speed against charted depth.

criticalSpeedWidth.source: Width of the depth-critical peak in depth Froude number

linearDerivativeFactor.source: Gives about 1.5 x at h/T 1.5 and 2.6 x at h/T 1.2, of the order of the Kijima et al. (1990) shallow-water corrections

crossFlowFactor.source: Gives about 3 x at h/T 1.2, as for ship sections approaching the bottom

addedMassFactor.source: Sway added mass about 2 x deep water at h/T 1.2

minimumDepthRatio.source: Keeps the corrections finite as depth approaches the draft; grounding is reported, not modelled

transverseMetacentricHeight.source: KB + BM_T - KG with demihull waterplanes at +/- half the separation

rollPeriod.source: 2 pi k_xx / sqrt(g GM_T) with k_xx about 0.4 B plus added inertia

pitchPeriod.source: 2 pi k_yy / sqrt(g GM_L) with k_yy about 0.25 L plus added inertia

heavePeriod.source: 2 pi sqrt((m + a_33) / (rho g A_wp)) with a_33 about m

rollDampingRatio.source: Catamaran roll is damped by the demihulls heaving in opposition

pitchDampingRatio.source: Pitch of slender high-speed hulls is heavily damped

heaveDampingRatio.source: Heave of slender high-speed hulls is heavily damped
